_description: Cross-SDK vectors for the opt-in mpa-v1 profile of multi-party authorization (spec/profiles/multi-party). Every evaluator MUST return each case's expect for records[record], under policy_sets[policy_set] and trust_sets[trust_set], for the operation, target and parameters in expected, at now_ms. expect.codes is the set of codes, sorted; no order among them is compared. Phases, each stopping the next when it adds a code: (1) structure, first failure only: the record conforms to multi_party_authorization.schema.json (MPA_SCHEMA_INVALID); operation_payload has a request member (MPA_REQUEST_MISSING) and conforms to multi_party_request.schema.json with RFC 3339 instants (MPA_REQUEST_INVALID); every number in it, read as the nearest binary64, is an integer from -(2^53 - 1) to 2^53 - 1, the integers a binary64 holds exactly, so it is representable in dcp-jcs-v1 and every implementation writes the same text for it (MPA_NOT_REPRESENTABLE), and it nests at most 32 levels deep, operation_payload being the first (MPA_NOT_REPRESENTABLE); at most 16 authorizations (MPA_TOO_MANY_AUTHORIZATIONS). (2) binding, every code: operation, request.target and the canonical form of parameters equal the expected ones (MPA_OPERATION_MISMATCH, MPA_TARGET_MISMATCH, MPA_PARAMETERS_MISMATCH); request.audience equals the policy set audience (MPA_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH); issued_at is not later than now plus 30 seconds (MPA_NOT_YET_VALID); expires_at is later than now (MPA_EXPIRED); expires_at is later than issued_at by at most max_validity_seconds (MPA_VALIDITY_INVALID); the policy set has a subject for request.target (MPA_TARGET_UNKNOWN) that lists the operation (MPA_OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED). (3) parties, every code: each party_id is a party of the subject (MPA_PARTY_UNKNOWN, and nothing else for that entry), appears once (MPA_PARTY_DUPLICATE), signed the role the operator gives it (MPA_ROLE_MISMATCH), and that role is allowed for the operation (MPA_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED). (4) verification, every code: binding pq_over_classical with a classical algorithm in the classical slot and a post-quantum one in the other (MPA_HYBRID_REQUIRED); each kid is a key of that party in the trust set with that algorithm (MPA_KEY_NOT_ANCHORED), not revoked (MPA_KEY_REVOKED), not expired (MPA_KEY_EXPIRED: status expired, or expires_at before now) and already valid (MPA_KEY_NOT_YET_VALID: not_before after now), the first of these per key; both signatures are canonical base64 and verify, the classical one over UTF8(context) || 0x00 || dcp-jcs-v1({operation, operation_payload, party_id, role}) and the post-quantum one over those bytes followed by the classical signature (MPA_SIGNATURE_INVALID). parties_counted is the number of authorizations with no code in this phase. (5) decision: parties_counted is at least the required_parties of the policy (MPA_THRESHOLD_NOT_MET) and every required role is held by a counted party (MPA_REQUIRED_ROLE_MISSING). authorized is true only when no phase added a code. The required_parties of the record never counts. verification is not_evaluated when phase 4 was not reached; required_parties is null when no operation rule was found. config_cases: loading policy_set MUST fail with expect_code, or succeed when it is null; a set with several problems is not among the cases. A required_parties above 16 is CONFIG_MPA_UNSATISFIABLE: a record holds at most 16 authorizations. trust_config_cases: loading trust_set with the principal trust set loader MUST fail with expect_code. Bounds (request_id 128, target and audience 256) count Unicode code points. Groups: controls are authorized; structure, binding, parties, signatures and threshold are refused by that phase; in binding, parties and threshold every signature verifies on its own; limits sit exactly on a bound, get past the structure phase and are refused by a later one. The evaluation is strict: an authorization that fails refuses the record even when the others meet the threshold.
_security_notice: The keys are derived from fixed strings in the generator. Test material only.
